https://www.dw.com/en/lebanon-says-11-ki.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5ItBR The Israeli strikes were the most deadly since a framework truce in June Image: Houssam Shbaro/Anadolu Agency/IMAGO Advertisement At least 11 people were killed when Israel launched fresh airstrikes in southern Lebanon on Saturday, the deadliest since the Israel-Hezbollah truce nearly two months ago. The attacks were met with defiance by the Iran-backed Hezbollah , which demanded an end to "humiliating" peace negotiations with Israel . What do we know? The Lebanese Health Ministry said one of the strikes, on the edge of the village of Ansar, killed seven people and wounded two. The dead included three children and two women, according to the ministry. The strike, which happened at dawn, hit a house and destroyed it, according to NNA, the Lebanese state news agency. Germany's DPA news agency cited residents as saying the property served as a base for Hezbollah. The Israeli strike on Ansar, in southern Lebanon, hit a house Image: Marwan Naamani/ZUMA/IMAGO The second strike hit the village of Deir al-Zahrani, killing four and wounding 17. NNA reported other strikes around the strategic Ali Taher hill, which overlooks parts of the southern city of Nabatiyeh and key roads to it. The Israeli military confirmed hitting Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, saying it was retaliation for an attack by the militia on Israeli forces. Hezbollah vows revenge Later Saturday, Hezbollah hit back at the latest strikes, saying they would be met with an "appropriate" response. Israel "must clearly understand that its attacks, violations and attempts to impose a fait accompli cannot continue, and will be met with an appropriate response", the Iran-backed group said in a statement. Hezbollah warned Lebanese authorities against continuing its "humiliating" negotiations with Israel, which would provide "the enemy with free concessions." Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam denounced the strikes, calling on Israel to "halt this escalation." "The seven martyrs of the Israeli airstrike on the town of Ansar are not military infrastructure and the children and women killed were not military targets,” he wrote on X. Hezbollah accused Israel of reigniting the war Image: Mohammed Zaatari/AP Photo/picture alliance Ceasefire struggles to stick The Israel–Hezbollah war reignited in early March around the start of the Iran war , when Hezbollah launched attacks on northern Israel to avenge the killing of Iran’s Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. It rapidly became a full-scale conflict that involved Israeli ground operations in southern Lebanon, mass evacuations of residents and the deaths of over 4,300 people. Israel claims to have established the so-called security zone in southern Lebanon to prevent Hezbollah attacks on northern Israel. According to Lebanese media, the Israeli-controlled area covers approximately 620 square kilometres, or about 6% of the country's total area. Israel and Hezbollah have repeatedly accused each other of ceasefire violations following the announcement of a framework peace agreement in late June, The deal lays out a plan for Israeli forces to withdraw from southern Lebanon , in return for Hezbollah laying down arms. It also envisions steps toward eventual peace. The two sides have held seven rounds of talks; the most recent in Rome earlier this month. Hezbollah refused direct talks, wasn't party to the deal and has refused to disarm. Edited by: Kieran Burke Don't let the algorithm hide the news. Beállítom Őrizetbe vett az osztrák rendőrség egy 49 éves magyar állampolgárt, akit azzal gyanúsítanak, hogy öt tartományban legalább 60 alkalommal tört fel autókat, illetve lopott el értékes járműalkatrészeket. A stájerországi rendőrség pénteki tájékoztatása szerint az okozott teljes kár több százezer euróra tehető. Az MTI azt írja, hogy a férfit tetten érték az alsó-ausztriai Brunn am Gebirgében, amikor egy autókereskedés területéről korábban leszerelt fénymodulokat és motorháztetőket vitt a közelben parkoló autójához. Csak ezzel az egy esettel mintegy 15 ezer eurós (kb. 5,5 millió forintos) kárt okozhatott. A nyomozás, amely útján a férfihoz eljutottak július 8-án indult, amikor egy grazi autókölcsönző telephelyén több járművet törtek fel. A grazi bűnügyi rendőrség ezután 60 ehhez hasonló esetet azonosított Stájerországban, Burgenlandban, Bécsben, Alsó-Ausztriában és Felső-Ausztriában. A nyomozók egy olyan jármű nyomára is bukkantak, amely több bűncselekménynél szerepet játszhatott – végül ennek segítségével jutottak el a magyar férfihoz. A gyanúsított Magyarországon már korábban is büntetést kapott vagyon elleni bűncselekmények miatt. Augusztus elején megállapították, hogy a férfi ismét Ausztriába érkezett, és többek között autókereskedések, valamint vállalati parkolók tűnt fel. Augusztus 18-án este a férfi ismét átlépte az osztrák határt a burgenlandi Klingenbachnál. A rendőrök egészen egy brunni ipari területig követték, ahol elektromos rollerrel felderítette a környéket. A következő éjszaka az alsó-ausztriai bevetési egység akkor csapott le rá, amikor a korábban leszerelt alkatrészeket az autójához vitte. A 49 éves férfi kihallgatásán csak a Brunn am Gebirge-i bűncselekményt ismerte el. A többi feltárt eset és az esetleges összefüggések vizsgálata továbbra is folyamatban van – közölte a Stájerországi Tartományi Rendőr-igazgatóság. https://www.mfa.gov.lv/en/article/foreig.text: Foreign Minister Baiba Braže to pay a working visit to Sweden Published: 25.08.2026. Photo: Laura Celmiņa, Ministry of Foreign Affairs Facebook X / Twitter Linkedin Threads On 26 August 2026, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Baiba Braže, will pay a working visit to Sweden. During the visit, the Minister will address Swedish ambassadors at a meeting, meet with Sweden's Minister of Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard to discuss current regional security and defence challenges, and will participate in the Women in Business working lunch for women business leaders. The Minister will also visit the defence and security company Scandinavian Astor Group, the Embassy of Latvia in Sweden, give an interview to the Swedish newspaper Svenska Dagbladet, and meet with representatives of the Latvian diaspora in Sweden. A joint press conference by the Latvian and Swedish Foreign Ministers will be streamed live at 12.30 (Latvian time) on the Swedish Ministry for Foreign Affairs’ YouTube channel.
